text: By far the larger part of the passers by wore a contented, business like look, as if their only thought were to make their way through the press of bodies. <break time="0.8s" /> Others, still a numerous class, moved restlessly and muttered to themselves, and if anyone jostled them, they bowed deeply to the offender as though overwhelmed with confusion. <break time="0.8s" /> There were clerks of every rank, the junior ones in tight coats and bright boots, the senior ones with slightly bald heads and right ears long accustomed to holding a pen. <break time="0.8s" /> Then came a race of well dressed pickpockets and gamblers, whose fine clothes and quick, watchful eyes betrayed the very trade they took such pains to conceal from the honest crowd. <break time="0.8s" /> Descending lower in the scale of humanity, I saw pale beggars, feeble invalids, and modest young girls returning from long labor, who shrank from the rude glances of passing ruffians. <break time="0.8s" /> There were also countless drunkards, some in rags and staggering, others still in decent clothes but with faces already marked by the slow ruin of drink and despair. <break time="0.8s" /> As the night deepened, the gas lamps, which at first had struggled feebly with the dying day, had at last gained the upper hand and threw over everything a fitful and garish luster. <break time="0.8s" /> With my brow pressed to the glass, I studied the faces one by one, and although the swiftness with which they passed allowed me only a glance, I seemed to read in each the history of long years.
